subject: HealthGrid procurement: marketplace vs PO — post-call action items
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@healthgrid.com>, procurement@healthgrid.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: HealthGrid procurement: marketplace vs PO — post-call action items

Hi Elena / HealthGrid procurement team,

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment on evaluation criteria and timing. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Recap (call highlights)
- HealthGrid evaluating AWS Marketplace Private Offer vs direct PO (card/PO) for initial pilot (analytics + embeddings).
- Procurement timeline estimated at ~3–6 weeks depending on internal approvals.
- Primary procurement asks: SOC 2 summary, vendor invoice sample, sample PO terms (net terms), and Master Services Agreement redlines.

Action items (owner / ETA)
1) From Redwood: share RFP response + SOC 2 summary + PO example (attached) — see attachments. (Mateo, by EOD today)
2) From HealthGrid: confirm preferred billing route (Marketplace private offer vs signed PO) and whether Treasury requires net-30 / PO prefix on invoice. (Elena, by next Wed)
3) Schedule procurement call to review PO language and invoice flow (tentative: Tue 10/06 09:30 PT). (All)

Checklist for procurement team to accelerate: 
- Decide billing platform: AWS Marketplace (Private Offer) or Redwood direct invoice (PO).
- Confirm billing legal entity + tax ID for invoice and W-9.
- Confirm whether HealthGrid needs us to sign an IP Addendum or specific data-processing terms beyond our standard MSA.

Attachments included: HealthGrid_RFP-Response.xlsx (summary of scope/pricing), SOC2_Summary.pdf (controls digest), PO-example.pdf (vendor PO template filled sample).

If Marketplace is easier for you, we can set up an AWS Private Offer (monthly billing) which often removes the need for a signed PO to start. If you need PO-first, we can accept net-30 on a signed PO — we'll need billing contacts and a purchase order number to generate invoices.

I'll follow up with Karthik (billing lead) on the exact mechanics so you have clear options for your finance team.

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: HealthGrid procurement: marketplace vs PO — post-call action items

Thanks Mateo — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- AWS Marketplace would be preferred by our Cloud team (makes chargeback and account mapping easier).
- Our procurement group still needs to evaluate pricing differences and any marketplace fee impact.
- Timeline: we should be able to get to an internal decision within ~3–4 weeks, but need to run pricing + PO requirements by Finance.

Can you send a short note on the expected delta between Marketplace list price vs direct PO pricing (if any) and confirm whether Redwood can provide a monthly invoice under a Private Offer? Also, please include the name/email of the Redwood billing contact so we can loop them in.

I’m available for the procurement call Tue 10/06 at 09:30 PT — booking now unless you prefer another time.

Best,
Elena Torres
Head of Procurement | HealthGrid
elena.torres@healthgrid.com

---
(Elena later added: We will also send over the SOC2 questionnaire and a draft PO template for your review before the call.)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@healthgrid.com>, procurement@healthgrid.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthGrid procurement: marketplace vs PO — post-call action items

Great — thanks Elena, appreciate the timeline. A few quick answers inline: 

- Delta on pricing: for most customers the AWS Marketplace Private Offer is price‑neutral to the direct PO price when arranged as a commercial private offer. We can provide the same unit pricing; marketplace fees are typically absorbed in the offer (we'll show exact numbers in the Private Offer).
- Monthly invoice under Private Offer: yes — we support monthly billing and can configure invoicing to your billing entity under a Private Offer.

Short recommendation: if your Cloud/FinOps team is comfortable with Marketplace, go that route to speed procurement and make chargebacks simpler. If Treasury requires a PO-first workflow for internal controls, we can accept a signed PO (net-30) and invoice against it — same onboarding, different billing path.

Prep for the procurement call (Tue 10/06 09:30 PT): 
- HealthGrid: send draft PO (if using PO) + any required billing entity details + SOC2 questionnaire answers you want us to see ahead of time.
- Redwood: Karthik will join to explain private offer mechanics and attach a PO example.

Karthik — can you add the quick bullets on marketplace mechanics for HealthGrid? I attached a PO-example.pdf they can use as a starting point.

Thanks — Mateo

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@healthgrid.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T17:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthGrid procurement: marketplace vs PO — post-call action items

Hi Elena / team,

Quick note from Redwood Finance / Billing: 

- AWS Marketplace Private Offer: we can publish a Private Offer with identical unit pricing to a direct contract. HealthGrid will see charges on their AWS invoice and AWS handles the billing/chargebacks to your org. Redwood will receive payment via AWS and settle with our finance team.
- Invoicing under Private Offer: AWS issues a consolidated invoice; if HealthGrid prefers direct invoicing we can instead accept PO+invoice net-30 on our Redwood billing (AP) terms.
- Tax/W-9: if you go direct PO route please send W-9 and billing entity details to enable our accounts receivable setup.
- Paperwork: MSA redlines are normal — we can sign an MSA + SOW. For faster start we can sign the MSA with standard data-processing terms and do a scoped SOW.

Tradeoffs to consider (short): 
- Speed: Marketplace Private Offer ≈ fastest (no PO waiting).
- Accounting: Direct PO gives you a vendor relationship and invoices come from Redwood (easier for some ERP setups).
- Fees: Private Offer normally neutral; confirm line-item if you need AWS payables to be shown differently.

I’ve attached PO-example.pdf as a sample. If you confirm you need net-30 PO flow, send the PO number + billing contact and we’ll spin up the AR record. Happy to join the procurement call tomorrow.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
